key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C self-fluxing coatings can be tuned from low-friction to high-wear-resistance behavior by adjusting barrel filling, O/C ratio, and inter-shot delay.
engineering_relevance: These results provide process windows for restoring and surface-hardening machine parts while balancing coating density, hardness, roughness, friction, and wear.
method: Adjusted working-gas molar ratio O/C from 1.026–1.856
evidence_signal: The abstract reports microstructural analysis plus tribological and mechanical testing, including friction coefficient, specific wear rate, roughness, and hardness, with best wear resistance at O/C = 1.856 and 1 s delay.
watch_item: Optimizing for minimum friction can increase wear, so implementation requires balancing competing tribological targets rather than selecting a single setting.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
